routes.description: Establish that morality includes objective value and categorical obligation, then explain those features and human moral knowledge through a transcendent divine ground.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if God supplies a coherent ground for objective moral facts, universal duties, human worth, and truth-directed moral cognition that secular goal-based ethics cannot supply.

motionBridge.description: Connect objective moral reality and universally binding duties to goodness grounded in a transcendent God.

centralBridges.description: Show that genuine moral obligations bind agents independently of whether they adopt human well-being as a goal.
Explain why human moral faculties can track real moral properties rather than merely adaptive or socially conditioned responses.
Ground human worth and rights in intentional creation rather than in contingent preferences or instrumental interests.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Account for cases in which self-interest or rejection of shared goals would permit profitable or concealed wrongdoing.
Distinguish the metaphysical grounding claim about God from reliance on a complete specifically Christian ethical code.

routes.description: Ground ethical deliberation in human interests, observable consequences, cooperation, and revisable public inquiry while challenging the content and justification of the proposed divine foundation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if secular humanism supplies fact-constrained methods for advancing human welfare and correcting error while the God proposal adds no demonstrated, coherent, or accessible ethical basis.

motionBridge.description: Connect shared human interests and observable consequences to a public, evidence-responsive foundation for ethical judgment.

centralBridges.description: Show that physical and social facts constrain better and worse means of advancing human well-being despite the goal's contingent adoption.
Provide evidence, consequences, consistency, and revision as mechanisms for identifying and correcting mistaken moral judgments.
Show that an unspecified God does not itself identify usable principles, duties, or agreed methods of resolving moral disagreement.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain human value through relationships, empathy, interdependence, and cooperation without requiring cosmic intrinsic value.
Test whether identifying God with goodness establishes the claimed foundation without circularity or unsupported inference.

sections.title: The content of an ethical foundation
sections.rationale: The comparison depends first on what morality requires and whether God or secular humanism supplies a sufficiently specified basis for those requirements.

sections.title: Conditional goals and categorical obligation
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether fact-sensitive pursuit of well-being can obligate unwilling agents or whether morality requires duties independent of adopted goals.

sections.title: Moral knowledge and error correction
sections.rationale: A foundation must explain how moral judgments connect to truth or better outcomes and how mistaken judgments can be recognized and revised.

sections.title: Human value, cooperation, and wrongdoing
sections.rationale: The rival foundations offer different accounts of human worth, cooperative motivation, and the constraint of conduct when personal advantage favors wrongdoing.

sections.title: Divine goodness and justificatory coherence
sections.rationale: The theistic route requires a coherent transition from objective morality to God while the secular challenge tests whether that transition is specified and noncircular.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: A genuine moral foundation must account for objective obligations, intrinsic values, responsibility, and moral improvement rather than redefine those phenomena.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: On a non-theistic evolutionary and social account, moral beliefs track survival or conditioning rather than moral facts, undermining trust in moral cognition.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Theism explains nonphysical moral properties and human access to them because a creator can ground goodness and authoritative obligations.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Goal-dependent ethics cannot bind people who reject universal well-being and can validate horrific means under vicious goals.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: A conditional route to well-being does not establish a moral obligation for a person who rejects human flourishing as a goal.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: Theism grounds human worth, moral obligation, and trust in moral experience by treating persons as intentionally created in God's image rather than as accidental organisms.

chunk-004:c004-03.proposition: A morality motivated by self-interest cannot forbid hidden wrongdoing when an agent expects personal benefit, no detection, and negligible wider consequences.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: Theism explains moral knowledge through reliable God-given faculties, while evolutionary wiring or social influence can cause moral beliefs without making them objectively true.

chunk-005:c005-03.proposition: God can be the necessary standard and ground of moral goodness independently of whether Christianity is the ethical system under discussion.

chunk-005:c005-04.proposition: Objective moral facts and universal obligations require a nonphysical, transhuman foundation, plausibly understood as goodness grounded in God's being.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: An unspecified God is an entity rather than an ethical system, and disagreement about divine identity, aims, and human interests prevents it from grounding ethics.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Morality can begin with contingent but shared concern for human well-being and objectively assess actions by their consequences for that agreed goal.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Invoking an unspecified creator does not establish objective moral truths or duties and therefore does not itself supply a foundation for ethics.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Mistaken or myopic conceptions of well-being can be exposed through internal conflict, consequences, and evidence without abandoning well-being as the standard.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: People enter the consequential conditions of social life without choosing them, so objective facts can establish better outcomes despite individual indifference.

chunk-004:c004-02.proposition: Concern for humans needs no divine basis, and enlightened self-interest can motivate cooperation because individual welfare depends on the welfare of others.

chunk-004:c004-08.proposition: Secular humanism uses empathy, education, evidence, and revision toward better outcomes, whereas objective imperatives and God remain undemonstrated.

chunk-005:c005-02.proposition: A generic deity supplies no ethical system, and appealing to specifically Christian commands exposes an unstable shift in the theistic case.

chunk-005:c005-05.proposition: Defining God as the standard of goodness is circular and does not demonstrate that objective moral facts possess a divine foundation.

chunk-005:c005-10.proposition: Human value need not be cosmic or intrinsic because interdependence, empathy, and cooperation justify valuing everyone while permitting reasonable personal priorities.
